originalTitle: SIF AUM jumps 29% to Rs 17,858 crore in June; inflows surge 171% MoM
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: Specialised Investment Funds (SIF) had a big increase in the amount of money they managed, with a 29% jump to Rs 17,858 crore in June. This happened because a lot more money was put into these funds, with inflows increasing by 171% compared to the previous month. One type of fund, called Hybrid Long-Short Funds, was particularly popular. The overall mutual fund industry also saw a lot of investor participation, with a record high in systematic investment plan (SIP) contributions. This suggests that individual investors are continuing to show strong interest in investing in mutual funds.

originalTitle: DMart Q1 results: Cons PAT up 11% to Rs 860 crore, revenue rises to Rs 18,795 crore
simplifiedContent: Here's what you need to know about DMart's recent performance: the company made an 11% more profit compared to the same time last year, with a total profit of Rs 860 crore. Their total sales, or revenue, also increased by 14.9% to Rs 18,795 crore. The company's operating profit, which is a measure of how efficiently they run their business, grew by 15.4%. This is good news for the company, and it shows that their business is doing well. This matters because it gives investors an idea of how well the company is performing, which can help them decide whether to invest in the company or not.

originalTitle: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
simplifiedContent: Foreign investors have taken out almost 60% of the money they had put into funds that focus on Indian stocks since the peak in 2024. This means they are moving their money to other investment opportunities, particularly in artificial intelligence. In 2026, they withdrew $9 billion from India-focused funds, showing a significant shift in their investment strategy. This change affects India-focused funds, but other types of investments, like gold and US stocks, have seen some new money coming in. Overall, foreign investors are rearranging their investments, pulling out of India-focused funds and putting money into other areas, including the US and Europe.

originalTitle: Nomura sees 22% upside in Ather Energy. Here's why it's the brokerage's top EV pick
simplifiedContent: Nomura, a big investment company, thinks Ather Energy's stock price will go up by 22% because they believe the company has a lot of growth potential. They are telling their clients to buy Ather Energy's stock, and they've raised their target price to ₹1,470. This means they think the stock will be worth ₹1,470 in the future. The reason for this prediction is that more people are expected to buy electric two-wheelers, and Ather Energy is well-placed to benefit from this trend. This is why Nomura thinks Ather Energy is a good investment opportunity, making it their top pick in the electric vehicle sector.

originalTitle: Why large cap and mid cap funds could be the best mutual fund to bet on now, according to Abakkus study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by Abakkus Mutual Fund suggests that large cap and mid cap funds could be a good investment option right now. This is because company earnings are improving and the prices of these funds are reasonable. The market has recently gone down, which means it could be a good time for long-term investors to get in. This is because stock prices may eventually catch up with the growing earnings of companies, making it a potentially good time to invest. Overall, this study thinks that large and mid cap funds could be a smart choice for investors looking to put their money into the market.

originalTitle: AI chip fever returns? SK Hynix  share price surges 13% after blockbuster $26.5 billion US listing
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, just listed its shares on the US stock market and raised a huge amount of money - $26.5 billion. The company's share price jumped 13% on its first day, which is a very strong start. This is significant because it shows that investors are very interested in companies that make chips used in artificial intelligence (AI). The demand for these chips is driving up their prices, which is good news for companies like SK Hynix. This surge in interest is happening even though the semiconductor industry has been a bit unpredictable lately.
